errors.meaning: The adapter was reached and failed.
A registry refused an image because this server, or the app's registry account, has downloaded too many images recently. The message says when it accepts downloads again, where the registry said.
The adapter needed for this is not configured or not reachable.
The credential presented is not valid.
No credential was presented, or the session has expired.
The token is unknown, revoked or expired.
The token's owner was suspended or deleted, so the token no longer resolves to anyone.
The password was right and the account has two-factor authentication. Sign in again with a code from its authenticator app, or one of its recovery codes, as `code`.
The backup could not be decrypted with the key supplied.
The backup is missing part of what it claims to hold, so it was not applied.
The build ran and did not succeed. Its log is the answer.
The built app listens only on 127.0.0.1 inside its container, where nothing outside it can reach it.
The build exceeded the time allowed for it.
Port-mode routing has no free port in the configured range.
Running this would commit more of the host than is left.
Pando failed in a way it did not expect. The request ID finds the log line.
No such object, or none the caller may see.
A change sent with a browser's Pando sign-in from a page on another origin, such as an app's. Send it from the console, or with an API token.
Authenticated, but not permitted to do this.
The app is shared with everyone who knows its passcode, and this request has not shown it. A browser is sent to the passcode page; entering it there lets the visitor in.
The account signed in with a password somebody else set, which must be changed first. Until it is, the session can only read its own account, change the password and sign out.
The caller holds no grant carrying the verb this action needs.
The spec names an adapter this installation does not have.
The spec asks for something the chosen adapter does not do.
The compose file uses a construct Pando will not translate.
The app loosens the installation's egress rules, and host policy says no app may.
The app's image has no build for the operating system and CPU architecture this server runs, so it cannot start here.
No configured adapter can satisfy this spec under host policy.
This installation requires a security score, and this app is below it or has never been scanned.
A required dependency has nothing filling it, so the deploy would start an app that cannot connect.
Host policy does not allow apps to be shared with everyone.
The person who would own the new app already owns as many apps as their limit allows. The message names the limit and where it is set.
Host policy requires a final backup before an app with storage is deleted, and the request said to delete without one.
Host policy has turned off terminal access, including for an app's owner.
Host policy does not allow apps from this source.
Host policy requires two-factor authentication for local accounts. An account without it can only set it up, and an account with it cannot turn it off.
A webhook points at a private, loopback or link-local address, and host policy does not allow that.
Too many wrong attempts in a short time, at a passcode or at sign-in. The message and the Retry-After header say how long to wait.
Another app is already reached at this address, or at a path this one would sit inside or around, or the address is Pando's own.
Another AI adapter already handles this AI function. Remove it from that adapter first.
The app started and then stopped, so the deploy has nothing to send traffic to.
The app has storage and the request did not say whether to keep a final backup of it.
The object is in a state this action does not apply to.
This is declared in Pando's startup configuration and cannot be changed through the API while it is.
Another account already has this username. A deleted account keeps its username, so it cannot be reused.
A workload mounts a volume the spec does not declare.
The spec refers to a slot it does not declare.
The workloads depend on each other in a cycle.
An environment variable is set twice with different values.
The request or spec is malformed.
A spec must name exactly one primary workload.
Pando could not read the repository: it is private or missing and no source connection covers it, or the connection's credential was refused.
A subscription names an event, or a pattern, that matches no event in the catalog.
